If an odor is coming from the sewer, then contact Dallas Water Utilities by calling 311 by phone instead of submitting a 311 request online. If you smell natural gas, then contact Atmos Energy or emergency dispatch.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request about current aggressive animal activity.
originalAction.why: Report a dog attacking a domestic animal or livestock, a loose aggressive animal, two or more dogs acting as an aggressive pack, or a high-risk dog active near children at an operating school, daycare, or park. The 311 request form asks where the animal was last seen, whether loose aggressive activity is currently in progress, whether the animal is owned, and how many animals are involved in pack or child-area incidents. It allows a past aggressive coyote incident.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Animal Aggressive Behavior" requests is not the route the Dallas 311 website gives for a human attack currently in progress, a human attacking an animal, a coyote attack in progress, a nonaggressive coyote sighting, or loose aggressive activity that is no longer in progress. If loose aggressive activity is no longer in progress, then submit an "Animal Loose" 311 request instead. If a nonaggressive coyote is being sighted, then call the Coyote Hotline. If a human attack or coyote attack is in progress, then call 911.
originalAction.how: Go to Dallas 311 > Choose "Animal Care and Control" > Choose "Animal Aggressive Behavior"
originalAction.how_formatted: [Go to Dallas 311](https://dallascrm.my.site.com/public/s/) > Choose "Animal Care and Control" > Choose "Animal Aggressive Behavior"

observations.value: Use this service request to report animal attacks, aggressive activity and aggressive pack activity on public or private property, school grounds, and day care centers. Service requests of this nature are dispatched and responded to based on priority. Priority 1: Instances in which a dog is attacking a domestic animal or livestock, an attack on a human and vice versa is currently in progress, or high-risk dogs are active near children or locations during operating hours where children are commonly present (example: schools, daycare facilities and parks) will be responded to within 1 hour. Priority 3: Instances in which two or more dogs act together as an aggressive pack will be responded to within 4 hours. Priority 4: Other instances of loose aggressive dogs will be responded to within 6 hours.

Animal attack to a human in progress and Human attacking an animal display “Emergencies of this nature should be reported to 911.” For loose aggressive animal, answer No to whether activity is in progress displays: “This request cannot be submitted on Animal Aggressive Behavior. Please choose Animal Loose to continue entering your request.” Selecting animal type Coyote displays the Coyote Hotline routing instruction: non-aggressive coyote/sighting call (469) 676-9813; attack in progress dial 911; continue if coyote is aggressive or attack occurred in the past. The Details form also says the responsible department may contact the requester and asks for name and phone number.
Activity = loose aggressive animal at school/park/daycare with children present OR aggressive pack activity

originalAction.why: Report a person bitten or scratched by an animal, an animal exposure, or a veterinary clinic request to pick up a bite-related rabies-testing specimen. The animal may be owned or unowned, loose or confined, and alive or deceased. The 311 request form asks for the victim, animal description, incident time and location, whether the biting animal is confined, and, for a deceased animal, its pickup location. Veterinary clinics use a distinct question path for specimen pickup.
originalAction.how: Go to Dallas 311 > Choose "Animal Care and Control" > Choose "Animal Bite"
originalAction.how_formatted: [Go to Dallas 311](https://dallascrm.my.site.com/public/s/) > Choose "Animal Care and Control" > Choose "Animal Bite"

observations.value: Use this service request to report that someone has been bitten or scratched by an animal. This service request can be entered whether or not the animal is owned. Veterinary clinics requesting rabies testing specimens may also enter their requests here due to them being bite related. Service requests of this nature are dispatched and responded to based on priority. Priority 3: Instances in which the biting animal remains loose will be responded to within 4 hours. Priority 3: Instances in which the biting animal has been contained will be responded to within 4 hours. Priority 5: Instances of rabies specimen pickups from Veterinary clinics will be responded to within 12 hours.

Clinic pickup = No adds gender, owned, where last seen, incident date/time, and current confinement questions; owned Yes adds where the animal lives. Clinic pickup = Yes hides gender, ownership, location last seen, incident time, confinement and location-of-animal questions, while retaining victim contact details, type of animal, animal description, and deceased question. Deceased Yes adds pickup-location yes/no and a required description of location; pickup-location Yes and No do not change the remaining fields. Scratch and Exposure showed the same form structure as Bite for both clinic answers. The page asks for requester name and phone for follow-up, but the Contact step specifically requires First Name, Last Name, and Email; Phone and Address were optional.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request for a confined animal.
originalAction.why: Report a confined stray cat, dog, livestock animal, or wild animal; examples include an animal in a vehicle or truck bed, a stray in a yard or humane trap, an animal trapped in a culvert, drain, or pipe, or a rabies-vector species such as a bat, fox, raccoon, skunk, or coyote confined in a home. The 311 request form distinguishes the confinement location, whether food, water, and protection from weather are available, whether an adult will be present, and whether an animal in a culvert or truck bed is in immediate danger.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Animal Confined" requests is not the recommended route for sick or injured wildlife, infant or juvenile wild animals, pets being surrendered by their owners, non-rabies-vector wildlife confined inside a home, or coyotes reported in the area. If a pet is being surrendered by its owner, then view the "Animal Owner Surrender" 311 guidance instead. If a wild animal is sick, injured, infant, or juvenile, then submit an "Animal Lack of Care" 311 request instead. If non-rabies-vector wildlife is confined inside a home, then consult BeDallas90.org/wildlife. If coyotes are being reported in the area, then call the Coyote Hotline.

Animals that can be safely transported can be brought to the animal shelter at 1818 N Westmoreland Rd during normal business hours. Visit https://dallascityhall.com/departments/dallas-animal-services/Pages/default.aspx for more details. Service requests of this nature are dispatched and responded to based on priority. Priority 2: Instances in which there exists an immediate threat to the life of the animal will be responded to within 2 hours. Priority 3: Instances in which an animal is confined within living quarters and is also of a species that commonly carries rabies (bats, coyotes, foxes, raccoons and skunks) will be responded to within 4 hours. Priority 5: Other instances of confined animals will be responded to within 12 hours.

Critical examples in the 311 request form include being hit by a car, active bleeding, exposed bone, unresponsiveness while breathing, little or no movement, or inability to walk on two or more legs. The 311 request form also covers an owned domestic animal left below 32 degrees Fahrenheit or during an active heat advisory, and asks about ownership, the animal’s location, and related care concerns such as tethering or unsanitary conditions.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Animal Lack of Care" requests is not the route the 311 request form gives for animal cruelty, and its extreme-temperature option applies only to owned domestic animals during an active heat advisory or temperatures below 32 degrees Fahrenheit. originalAction.why: To request removal of litter along a street, median, sidewalk, or highway right-of-way on public property within Dallas or an external partner right-of-way such as TxDOT or the North Texas Toll Authority. The 311 request form asks whether the location is public or private, where litter is located, and its direction of travel; for an unlisted direction, it asks for a description.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Clean Sweep! Litter Removal" requests does not apply to alleyways, litter on private property, or homeless encampments. If litter is on private property, then submit a "Code Concerns" 311 request instead. If the concern is a homeless encampment, then submit a "Homeless Encampment" 311 request instead.

[Go to Dallas 311](https://dallascrm.my.site.com/public/s/) > Choose "ADA/Fair Housing Complaints" > Choose "Fair Housing Complaint"

Responsible recipient: Office of Housing and Community Empowerment
input.why: Report alleged discrimination in the sale, rental, or financing of housing based on sex, color, race, religion, disability, familial status, national origin, or another reason offered in the 311 request form. The 311 request form also covers retaliation for filing a Fair Housing complaint or contacting Code Enforcement, asks who allegedly discriminated and where it occurred, and offers an ADA-concerns option.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request for a Dallas Fire-Rescue safety education program.
originalAction.why: To request a fire-safety educational program or training, such as a fire safety house, fire brigade training, high-rise or home fire safety, programs for hospitals, nursing homes, hotels or schools, safety fairs, senior talks, Sparky, or extinguisher training. The 311 request form asks for the program type and can collect occupancy type, audience age group, and preferred date and time.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Fire Department Educational Request" requests does not apply to a fire-station visit or having a fire engine at a location. If you want a station visit or an engine on location, then email Dallas Fire-Rescue at dfrshowandtell@dallasfire.gov.
originalAction.how: Go to Dallas 311 > Choose "Non-Emergency Police and Fire Services" > Choose "Fire Department Educational Request"
originalAction.how_formatted: [Go to Dallas 311](https://dallascrm.my.site.com/public/s/) > Choose "Non-Emergency Police and Fire Services" > Choose "Fire Department Educational Request"

observations.value: Use this service request to request fire safety educational programs only. Requests to visit a fire station or to have an engine on location must be submitted to the following email address: dfrshowandtell@dallasfire.gov. originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request to clean a public inlet, storm drain, drainage ditch, or City-maintained culvert.
originalAction.why: For cleaning an inlet or storm drain on public property or a drainage easement, including debris, dirt, grass, or leaves. Dallas Water Utilities also maintains storm sewer lines and removes obstructions in culverts under City-maintained streets and alleys. The 311 request form asks whether the street or alley is flooded, the kind of cleaning or repair needed, the drain contents, and the location.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Inlet/Storm Drain Cleaning" requests does not apply to a flooded street or alley, an animal or personal item or smoke in an inlet or storm drain, or cleaning on private property. If the street or alley is flooded, then call 311 by phone instead of submitting a 311 request online for the hazardous stopped-up condition. If an animal or personal item is in the inlet or storm drain, then call 311 by phone instead of submitting a 311 request online about the hazardous objects-dropped service. If smoke is in the inlet or storm drain, then call 311 by phone instead of submitting a 311 request online. If an inlet is in an apartment-complex parking lot, then notify apartment management or maintenance.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request to receive advance mosquito-spraying notifications as a beekeeper.
originalAction.why: For a beekeeper, meaning a person who keeps, raises, and cares for honeybees, to provide contact information so the City of Dallas can notify them before ground or aerial mosquito-abatement spraying. The 311 request form asks the property type and whether notice is wanted for aerial spraying, ground spraying, or both. The 311 request form says the City gives 4–7 hours of advance notice for ground spraying and 12–24 hours for aerial spraying. Ground spraying requires an email address; the aerial-spraying choice allows Email or Phone, while choosing Both collects an email address.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Mosquito Beekeeper Notification" requests does not apply to complaints about bees or concerns about mosquitoes. If you need pest control for bees, then contact a private exterminator. If the concern is mosquitoes, then submit a "Code Concerns" 311 request instead and select pest/bugs.
originalAction.how: Go to Dallas 311 > Choose "City Code Violations" > Choose "Mosquito Beekeeper Notification"
originalAction.how_formatted: [Go to Dallas 311](https://dallascrm.my.site.com/public/s/) > Choose "City Code Violations" > Choose "Mosquito Beekeeper Notification"

observations.value: This Service Request is used to COLLECT Beekeeper contact information. A Beekeeper is defined as a person who keeps, raises, and cares for honeybees. This Service Request will allow the City of Dallas to provide "notification" to Beekeepers before ground and aerial spraying take place for mosquito abatement. The City of Dallas does not respond to complaints regarding bees, please contact a private exterminator for pest control. If the concern is regarding mosquitoes, please submit a Code Concern Service Request Type (and select pest/bugs). The estimated response time for this service request is 48 hours.

The City will contact you 4-7 hours prior to ground spraying and 12-24 hours prior to aerial spraying via email. Property type options did not reveal additional fields. Ground spraying directly adds a required email address. Aerial spraying adds a required preferred-method radio: Email adds a required email field; Phone adds no Details fields. Both adds a required email field and no preferred-method question. Contact-preference options did not change the form.

This Service Request will allow the City of Dallas to provide "notification" to Beekeepers before ground and aerial spraying take place for mosquito abatement. The City of Dallas does not respond to complaints regarding bees, please contact a private exterminator for pest control. If the concern is regarding mosquitoes, please submit a Code Concern Service Request Type (and select pest/bugs). The estimated response time for this service request is 48 hours.

The City will contact you 4-7 hours prior to ground spraying and 12-24 hours prior to aerial spraying via email. Property type options did not reveal additional fields. Ground spraying directly adds a required email address. Aerial spraying adds a required preferred-method radio: Email adds a required email field; Phone adds no Details fields. Both adds a required email field and no preferred-method question. Contact-preference options did not change the form.

originalAction.why: To report chronic or recurring noise at the same residential location, such as ongoing loud music or disturbances. The 311 request form asks whether the problem recurs, what the noise is, and which days or times it occurs.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Noise Complaint (Residential)" requests does not apply to noisy animals, construction noise, noise at clubs or bars, a first-time report at a location, or noise occurring now. If the concern is construction noise or noise at a club or bar, then submit a "Code Concerns" 311 request instead. If the concern is a noisy animal, then view the "Animal - Noisy" 311 guidance instead. If this is the first report at that location, then call 911 instead of submitting a 311 request online. If the noise is occurring now, then call 911 instead of submitting a 311 request online.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request for residential storm brush and debris.
originalAction.why: Report storm brush and debris at a residence after a recent storm, including heavy rain, thunderstorms, wind, or ice. The 311 request form asks whether debris blocks a street or alley and says storm brush and debris should be moved to the front parkway. Sanitation uses the request to assess damage and where collection efforts are most needed.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Report Storm Brush/Debris" requests does not apply to downed trees, electrical lines, power outages, or storm debris blocking a street or alley. Pickup before the regular bulk trash week and a hold on bulk trash citations are not guaranteed. If a tree or limb blocks a street or alley, then call 311 by phone to report the concern to Public Works instead of submitting a 311 request online. originalAction.why: For a residential Sanitation customer claiming the annual exemption for an oversized brush or bulk setout of no more than 20 cubic yards. observations.value: Use this service request for residential customers to claim their annual oversized brush/bulk collection not to exceed 20 cubic yards. The service request must be submitted the week prior to the scheduled brush/bulk collection week (customers can not use this Service Request type to replace a Cost-Plus request). An excessive fee of $60 per five cubic yards will be directly billed to the customer's Dallas Water Utilities account if the debris set out is more than the monthly 10 cubic yards without the annual oversized exemption service request, or if the annual oversized exemption is more than 20 cubic yards. A resident is also subject to a Citation issued by Code Compliance for violating the limit size (City Code Sec. 18-4 (h)(3)). For more information on the new brush/bulk regulations, please Click Here.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request for pickup of a deceased animal.
originalAction.why: For removal of a deceased animal from an eligible location, such as a street, sidewalk, alley, lot, apartment complex, or private property. The 311 request form asks where it is, species, ownership, bite or physical-contact history, suspected intentional violence, and whether it is in the Dowdy Ferry/Teagarden area. Private-property pickup by Dallas Animal Services requires the customer to be over 65 or physically disabled, provide a contact number, and be present. An animal over 100 pounds on private property carries a $125 charge to the Dallas Water Utilities account.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Sanitation Dead Animal Pick Up" requests cannot continue for freeway or freeway-median locations, an animal that bit someone in the last 10 days, physical contact with a coyote, fox, raccoon, skunk, or bat, or an animal in the Dowdy Ferry/Teagarden area. Private-property pickup is limited to customers over 65 or physically disabled who can provide a contact number and be present; this service is not the directed route for a sick or injured living animal or suspected intentional violence. If an animal bit someone recently or one of the listed wild animals was touched, then submit an "Animal Bite" 311 request instead. If the animal is sick or injured, then submit an "Animal Lack of Care" 311 request instead. If intentional violence may have caused the death, then call 911. If the location is a freeway or freeway median, then contact TxDOT.

Use this service request to request repairs/replacements or delivery of roll carts. For RESIDENTIAL CUSTOMERS ONLY, use to request new roll cart service (no roll carts are on property) or the additional/removal of a roll cart(s). All customers (Commercial/Business, Residential, or Multi-Family) can also use this request for the maintenance of existing roll cart(s). The fee for each additional residential garbage roll cart is $15.51. Effective October 1, 2023, the owner or occupant of a dwelling unit with one roll cart for recyclable materials may request one additional roll cart for recyclable materials from the director of sanitation for no additional fee. Dwelling units with two or more roll carts for recyclable materials may request additional roll carts for recyclable materials for a one-time processing and handling fee for $50.00 per roll cart, which will be applied to the dwelling unit’s water account. The estimated response time for a request of this nature is 2 business days.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request for missed residential brush or bulk collection.
originalAction.why: Report a residential brush or bulk collection that was missed, including brush or tree limbs, bagged yard waste, eligible appliances, or furniture. The 311 request form asks whether this is a business or residence, whether 6:00 P.M. Friday of the scheduled collection week has passed, whether an Orange Tag is present, and what items are out. Sanitation may still collect through that Friday cutoff.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Sanitation Missed Brush/Bulk" requests does not apply to business or commercial accounts or a pickup week that has not passed its 6:00 P.M. Friday cutoff. Orange-tagged items require the collection violation to be corrected, and appliances with Freon, construction debris, mirrors or glass, electronics, tires, car parts, and machinery containing gasoline are not accepted curbside. If a business needs to dispose of brush or bulk items, then self-transport them to McCommas Bluff Landfill or one of the three transfer stations. If an Orange Tag identifies a collection violation, then correct the violation before the next scheduled collection attempt.
originalAction.how: Go to Dallas 311 > Choose "Garbage, Recycle, and Brush/Bulky Item Collection" > Choose "Sanitation Missed Brush/Bulk"
originalAction.how_formatted: [Go to Dallas 311](https://dallascrm.my.site.com/public/s/) > Choose "Garbage, Recycle, and Brush/Bulky Item Collection" > Choose "Sanitation Missed Brush/Bulk"

observations.value: Use this service request to report a missed residential brush/bulk collection. Sanitation Services has until 6:00 P.M. on the Friday of the scheduled collection week to pick up brush/bulk debris from the service location. If you have received an Orange Tag on your brush/bulk debris, a collection violation was identified and needs to be corrected in order for your location to be serviced. Collection will be attempted on your next scheduled day of service or week. Visit DallasCityHall.com/Sanitation to Contact Us online or by phone. Business/Commercial accounts are not currently serviced for brush/bulk collections. The estimated initial response time for a service request of this nature is 2 business days. Missed bulk/brush service is resolved within 7 business days.

Business/Commercial accounts are not currently serviced for brush/bulk collections. Customers needing to dispose of brush and/or bulk items can also self-transport to the McCommas Bluff Landfill or one of the three transfer stations. Visit DallasCityHall.com/Sanitation for more information.

What does NOT go on the curb? Construction debris (e.g. bricks, concrete, rocks, dirt, etc,), mirrors and glass (e.g. windows or shower glass), electronics (e.g. televisions, computers, etc.), tires (passenger tires 25 inches or less can be taken to the Landfill or the Northwest Transfer Station. Please limit to 6 per year per resident), Car parts (e.g. engine), and lawnmowers or any machinery containing gasoline.

If you have received an Orange Tag on your brush/bulk debris, a collection violation was identified and needs to be corrected in order for your location to be serviced. Collection will be attempted on your next scheduled day of service or week. Visit DallasCityHall.com/Sanitation to Contact Us online or by phone.

As a reminder, Sanitation Services has until 6:00 P.M. on the Friday of the scheduled collection week to pick up brush/bulk debris from the service location. If it is currently before 6:00 P.M. on that Friday, Sanitation Services may still be picking up collections.
What brush/bulk items do you have out for pickup?

[Go to Dallas 311](https://dallascrm.my.site.com/public/s/) > Under "Other Requests", choose "Storm Drainage/Flooding Complaint"

Responsible recipient: Dallas Water Utilities
input.why: For nonemergency flooding from rising water in a creek or street overflow caused by inadequate drainage capacity within the City service area. The 311 request form asks whether an inlet, drain, or culvert may need cleaning, whether water is moving or standing, whether flooding is happening now, and whether water has entered a building.
input.whyNot: The online form for "Storm Drainage/Flooding Complaint" requests is described for nonemergency concerns only and displays a jurisdiction alert for a location outside the City service area.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request for street, pedestrian, or highway lighting maintenance.
originalAction.why: To report maintenance needed for street, pedestrian, highway, or freeway lighting, including high mast and underpass lights. The 311 request form covers a bulb that is out, a light cycling on and off, a knocked-down pole, a row of lights out, or another lighting problem; a pole number can be supplied if available.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Street Lamp/Light Maintenance" requests is not the route for lights on wooden poles, traffic signals, school flashers, or warning flashers. If the issue concerns a traffic signal, school flasher, or warning flasher, then call 311 by phone instead of submitting a 311 request online. If the street light is mounted on a wooden pole, then report it directly to Oncor.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request for hazardous debris blocking a public right of way.
originalAction.why: Report hazardous spills or debris blocking a public right of way, street, alley, sidewalk, driving lane, or other travel lane. The 311 request form asks what debris is present, whether a Sanitation truck caused the spill, and, for street or freeway locations, the direction of travel and affected lane.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Street Spillage/Debris in Right of Way" requests is not the directed route for nonblocking litter or debris on a grassy or dirt roadside area; freeway routing is ambiguous because the description for "Street Spillage/Debris in Right of Way" requests on the Dallas 311 website assigns responsibility to TxDOT while the 311 request form still offers Freeway as a location. If a Sanitation truck caused property damage, then submit a "Sanitation Property Damage" 311 request instead. If litter or debris is on a grassy or dirt area without blocking a travel lane, then submit a "Median/Right of Way Maintenance" 311 request instead. If the concern is on a freeway, then contact TxDOT.
originalAction.how: Go to Dallas 311 > Choose "Environmental Quality Concerns" > Choose "Street Spillage/Debris in Right of Way"
originalAction.how_formatted: [Go to Dallas 311](https://dallascrm.my.site.com/public/s/) > Choose "Environmental Quality Concerns" > Choose "Street Spillage/Debris in Right of Way"

observations.value: Use this service request to report hazardous spills or debris blocking the public right-of-way to include driving or travel lanes of traffic. ** Freeways are the responsibility of Texas Dept. of Transportation (TXDOT). ** The estimated response time (ERT) for this service request is 12 hours.

Please verify the debris/spillage is blocking the driving/travel lanes of traffic or public right of way causing a hazard. If litter/debris is on the grassy/dirt area alongside or within a highway/freeway, street or intersection please create a Median/Right of Way Maintenance SR - this work is performed by City crews and a private contractor.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request for debris sweeping on a major thoroughfare.
originalAction.why: For routine sweeping of dirt, leaves, mud, rocks, sand, small tree twigs, or another debris type along a major Dallas thoroughfare. The 311 request form asks whether the street is a major thoroughfare or residential and, for a major thoroughfare, what debris is present; city routes are swept about once a month, weather permitting.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Street Sweeping - Thoroughfares" requests is not for residential streets, private property, or parking lots. If a hazard such as glass or other harmful debris is on a residential street, then call 311 by phone instead of submitting a 311 request online, and ask about "Street Spillage/Debris in Right-of-Way - Hazardous".
originalAction.how: Go to Dallas 311 > Choose "Streets, Medians, Sidewalks and Alleys" > Choose "Street Sweeping - Thoroughfares"
originalAction.how_formatted: [Go to Dallas 311](https://dallascrm.my.site.com/public/s/) > Choose "Streets, Medians, Sidewalks and Alleys" > Choose "Street Sweeping - Thoroughfares"

observations.value: Use this request to report sweeping needed on major thoroughfares ONLY, no residential streets, private property or parking lots. If a Hazard (such as, glass or other harmful debris) exists on a residential street call 3-1-1 and refer to Street Spillage/Debris in Right-of-Way – Hazardous, and city crews will respond. The estimated response time (ERT) for this service request is 3 business days. NOTE: Sweeping is completed once a month along the scheduled route, weather permitting. The city has a systematic cleaning schedule that covers all major traffic thoroughfares within Dallas. Cleaning includes sweeping along the curb line at each location.
The city does not provide street sweeping on residential streets, private property or parking lots.

members.title: Traffic Signal Maintenance - Report a Problem

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request for a non-emergency traffic signal problem.
originalAction.why: For a non-emergency signal issue such as one burned-out bulb, a partially blocked signal, a broken or missing pedestrian crossing button, or graffiti on a signal sign or control box. The 311 request form asks which signal concern occurred and collects details such as the affected bulb or lane, street and travel direction, obstruction cause, graffiti location, or crossing direction.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Traffic Signal Maintenance - Report a Problem" requests does not apply to a burned-out red bulb when fewer than two signal heads are visible in the same direction of travel, school-zone flasher issues, traffic-signal timing or sync issues, or requests to install a new pedestrian crossing button. If graffiti is on a signal pole, then consider the "Code Concerns" 311 request suggested by the Dallas 311 website. If the issue is a school-zone flasher, then submit a "School Zone Flasher Maintenance" 311 request instead. If the request is for a new pedestrian crossing button or signal timing/modification, then submit a "Traffic Signal Timing and Modification" 311 request instead. If a red signal bulb is burned out and fewer than two signal heads are visible in the same direction of travel, then call 311 by phone instead of submitting a 311 request online and report a "Traffic Signal Head Turned or Not Visible" concern.
originalAction.how: Go to Dallas 311 > Choose "Traffic Signs and Signals" > Choose "Traffic Signal Maintenance - Report a Problem"

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request to locate traffic-signal or street-lighting lines before excavation.
originalAction.why: For locating buried traffic-signal, pedestrian-signal, flasher, message-sign, communication, or street-lighting infrastructure before boring or trenching near a street or easement. The description asks for the 811 request email confirmation and work-site photos or a marked map. The 311 request form asks for excavator and site contacts, work scope and depth, marked area, cross streets, and whether the locate is emergency, mark-and-go, or a scheduled meeting.
originalAction.how: Go to Dallas 311 > Choose "Traffic Signs and Signals" > Choose "Traffic Signals and Lighting - Line Locate"
originalAction.how_formatted: [Go to Dallas 311](https://dallascrm.my.site.com/public/s/) > Choose "Traffic Signs and Signals" > Choose "Traffic Signals and Lighting - Line Locate"

observations.value: Use this service request to request a traffic signaling (pedestrian and vehicle signals, flashers, message signs, signal communication) or street lighting line-locate at an intersection or within a street block. A line-locate is most often needed when construction requires a vertical bore/trench or a horizontal bore/trench. Any activity that requires digging near a street or easement shall have a line-locate prior to digging. Line-locates are occasionally requested so that construction can proceed without impacting existing infrastructure. *** Upload the 811 request email confirmation and photos of work site or marked up map where line-locates are requested *** The estimated response time (ERT) for this service request is 5 business days.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request to study traffic-speed control for a Dallas street.
originalAction.why: For excessive speed, pedestrian or bicycle safety, cut-through traffic, crashes, or quality-of-life concerns on a street, including possible road or speed humps, street markings, bicycle lanes, or speed trailers. The 311 request form asks whether the area is residential or commercial/industrial, lane count, location along the roadway, crosswalk impact, weekdays or weekends, time of day, and whether construction contributes. Intersections should be entered in alphabetical order. The description says a study and petition are required when requesting speed-control measures; a name, address, and phone number are required.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Traffic - Speed Control" requests does not apply to chronic or recurring speeding or traffic violations. If the concern is chronic or recurring speeding or another traffic violation, then submit a "Chronic Traffic Violations" 311 request instead. If you want additional police patrol in a neighborhood or Dallas area, then submit an "Increased Police Patrol" 311 request instead.

originalAction.why: For a utility-service complaint or information request, such as a high bill, service quality, disconnected or unavailable service, or another concern, or for utility equipment in a street or alley such as wires on the ground, damaged poles or boxes, work-crew debris, graffiti, leaning poles, low wires, open trenches, or tree limbs in utility lines. If a street light is mounted on a wooden pole, then report it directly to Oncor. If the street light is not mounted on a wooden pole, then submit a "Street Lamp/Light Maintenance" 311 request instead.

Billing examples include a bill not received or a request to explain charges; payment questions can identify the payment date and method, such as automatic draft, online bank or City water e-pay, phone, mail, drop box, pay station, walk-in, or courier. originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Water Payments & Billing Inquiry" requests is not for water service restoration, discontinuance, new service, theft of water, or garbage pickup questions. If the question is about garbage pickup, then call 311 by phone instead of submitting a 311 request online. If the concern involves service restoration, discontinuance, new service, or theft of water, then call Water Customer Service at 214-651-1441.

originalAction.tagline: Submit a 311 request for a routine public water or wastewater line locate in Dallas.
originalAction.why: Request a routine locate of a public Dallas Water Utilities water or wastewater line for one location in a single service request; the work is handled as a "Mark and go" locate. The 311 request form asks whether the work area is marked or white-lined, the Mapsco location, and the company name. It warns that an unmarked area may delay the locate or reduce its accuracy. The request is scheduled and closed within one business day, after which Dallas Water Utilities has three additional business days to complete the locate.
originalAction.why_not: The online form for "Water/Wastewater Line Locate" requests does not apply to private-system locations, water lines outside the City of Dallas, or more than one location per service request. If the water lines are outside the City of Dallas, then call 8-1-1.
